text:
Buffalo needed one period to settle this. In the second, the Sabres scored three times in just over six minutes, with Rasmus Dahlin's slap shot making it 3-1, Josh Norris adding his second of the night and Josh Doan deflecting one in to make it 5-1. Columbus never recovered, and the Sabres won 5-2 at KeyBank Center, getting a little back after losing 6-3 to the Blue Jackets on October 1.

Norris was the one to watch. He scored twice in 13 minutes of ice time, and Buffalo had the better of the chances whenever he was out there. He came into the league as the 19th pick in 2017 and put up 19 points in 17 games at Michigan before turning pro. Owen Power set up three goals from the blue line, and Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen stopped 24 of 26 shots. By our numbers that was about one goal better than the chances he faced deserved, which matters in a game Columbus did get a few looks in.

Buffalo also played the better game. The Sabres out-chanced Columbus 4.16 to 3.12 in expected goals, a measure of shot quality, and in the second period it was 2.21 to 0.94. Our simulations of every shot give Buffalo a 65% chance to win a replay, so the lead was earned. Dahlin's goal came on a 3% chance, which was the lucky one. Columbus pushed in the third, with Mathieu Olivier a 49% chance stopped by Luukkonen, and Zach Werenski scored on the power play with under two minutes left. It came too late to matter, and Jet Greaves faced 37 shots in the loss.
